decisions.quote: What we may conclude, therefore, is that the effect of eye primes on prosocial behavior does not generalize from the settings used by Haley and Fessler [21] and Bateson, Nettles, and Roberts [22]. Our failure to find an effect is informative about the actual overall effect size, and the conditions in which it occurs [32].
decisions.location: Primary Discussion, original-specific generalisation verdict; Methods and reference22 independently inspected
decisions.reason: The primary Methods deliberately combine Haley/Fessler eye cues and Bateson/Nettle/Roberts eyes-versus-flowers control, and Discussion explicitly judges generalisation from BOTH earlier settings using its new empirical allocation experiment. The printed reference gives Bateson2006 Cues of being watched enhance cooperation in a real-world setting. Bateson is the separate honesty-box field experiment described in the Introduction, not an alternate report of shipped Haley/Fessler2005 laboratory game. All supplied shipped identities contain only Haley/Fessler, so this specific conceptual-retest pair is genuinely absent. Do not infer every possible background eye-prime citation as another target.
